name: Andreessen Horowitz (LLMflation, CIO survey, Top 100)
reason: Episodic essays and surveys, not refreshable series; a figure enters as a manual row when an indicator needs it.

name: Bain & Company technology report
reason: Annual report; its revenue-needed claim sits on the prediction ledger with its own URL.

name: Sequoia (David Cahn, AI's $600B question)
reason: A framework, not a series; the ratio it argues about is computed from filings (capex_to_revenue_stack).

name: Goldman Sachs Top of Mind
reason: Client research; the public issue is a claim on the prediction ledger.

name: J.P. Morgan Eye on the Market (Michael Cembalest)
reason: Commentary that cites filings the tracker ingests directly.

name: Citi and Barclays research
reason: Client research behind a wall.

name: Bloomberg circular-deals graphic
reason: Paywalled graphic; each deal on the circular ledger enters from its own filing or announcement instead.

name: Carta (Peter Walker) data posts
reason: Cohort benchmarks across Carta's customers, not sub-layer series.

name: Bessemer and ICONIQ state-of-AI reports
reason: Portfolio benchmarks published annually, not refreshable series.

name: Air Street Capital State of AI
reason: Annual report; single figures enter as manual rows when an indicator needs one.

name: SVB state of the markets
reason: Aggregate venture commentary; the tracker counts rounds bottom-up from Form D and Epoch.

name: NVCA-PitchBook Venture Monitor
reason: Aggregate US venture totals behind a registration wall; the tracker counts rounds bottom-up.

name: OECD.AI venture data (Preqin)
reason: Country aggregates; the macro share of AI venture reaches the tracker through OWID.

name: Stanford HAI AI Index
reason: Annual; its charts reach the tracker through OWID, and single figures enter as manual rows.

name: aifunding.me round tracker
reason: Planned third round source for venture flows; not wired, so round coverage stays Form D plus Epoch.

name: MultiState and Transparency Coalition bill trackers
reason: Overlap NCSL's count; a fetched count would be state_ai_bills_introduced's second source when one is published without a login.

name: EU AI Office
reason: No numeric series the diffusion lens scores.

name: ITjuzi, 36Kr, Zero2IPO, SCMP, Caixin
reason: Paywalled or Chinese-language compilations; the Chinese labs' rounds come through Epoch.

name: SEC 13F holdings
reason: Forty-five-day lag and no indicator needs institutional marks.

name: HKEX filings (Zhipu, MiniMax)
reason: No connector; the Chinese labs' run-rates come through Epoch.

attribution: Trajectory (Ronak Malde, Arjun Karanam, Michael Elabd)
name: Trajectory field notes
reason: Read for the continual-learning ladder; the Trajectory rung quotes Baseten's post about it, so no figure is taken from this page yet.

attribution: Joy Larkin, cleverhack.com trackers and Awesome-AI-Market-Maps
name: cleverhack.com AI lab trackers and Awesome-AI-Market-Maps
reason: Category directories, not data (P1 §5.3). The neolab directory seeded the neolabs sub-layer's entity list on 11 Sep 2026; the frontier tracker's lab list overlaps the seed list; the coding landscape mixes models, agents, IDEs and benchmarks, so it is not mapped.

name: PitchBook (paid)
reason: Paid; the stub refuses to run without PAID_SOURCES and a key. Would unlock market-wide round coverage, stage mix and median round size.

name: Crunchbase (paid)
reason: Paid; stub off. Would unlock founding dates and stage labels.

name: SemiAnalysis (paid)
reason: Paid; stub off. Would unlock the GPU rental index and unit inference costs (the app model tax).

name: The Information (paid)
reason: Paid; stub off. Would unlock app-layer financials.

name: Dealroom API (paid)
reason: Paid; stub off. Dealroom's public news pages are read as a manual source.

name: CB Insights (paid)
reason: Paid; stub off.

name: Sacra (paid)
reason: Paid; stub off. Would unlock private revenue estimates for app-layer valuation multiples.

name: Caplight (paid)
reason: Paid; stub off. Would unlock secondary marks between rounds.

name: X embed endpoint (oEmbed)
reason: X's robots.txt disallows its embed endpoint, so the tracker makes no request to X; posts by people it reads are quoted from pages that already carry their text, with the X link kept.

name: X API (curated List)
reason: Paid API; posts are quoted from pages that already carry their text instead.

name: Tracxn
reason: Login and paid tiers; no free data path.

name: Forge, EquityZen and Notice (secondary marks)
reason: Secondary-market marks sit behind accounts and paid tiers; the indicator that would use them stays unpublished.

name: Axios Pro Rata
reason: An email newsletter; the deals database behind it is paid.

name: Newcomer and Paul Kedrosky (Substack)
reason: Substack refuses the nightly's cloud fetches, so a feed row would fail every night; read by hand.

name: Tomasz Tunguz (blog)
reason: Commentary rather than data; his infrastructure-to-revenue claim is on the prediction ledger.

name: Allianz Research
reason: Occasional PDFs with no series; quoted by hand when a figure is needed.

name: Epoch AI GPU clusters and data centres
reason: No indicator uses them yet; a table reader is a short addition to the Epoch connectors when one does.

name: BLS Occupational Employment and Wage Statistics
reason: Annual and about eleven months late; the monthly labour trackers cover the same occupations sooner.

name: Stanford GDP-B (consumer surplus)
reason: Read through the Stanford Digital Economy Lab rows (consumer surplus and willingness to accept), not a separate feed.

name: IDC and Synergy Research (cloud and AI market shares)
reason: Paid; press-release headlines only, so cloud share comes from filings instead (P1 §5.2, §6.1).

name: AI as Normal Technology (essays and newsletter)
reason: Their claims are on the prediction ledger and their 89 named bottlenecks on /bottlenecks; the essays are read by hand, not ingested.

name: Capability and timelines writers
reason: Essays and posts read by hand for claims and leads; a figure they cite enters only from its primary source.

name: Labour-market economists
reason: Papers and posts read by hand; figures enter through the trackers and papers they publish (Lucy Wark's affiliation is to verify).

name: Semiconductor, cloud and software analysts
reason: Newsletters and notes read by hand; most are paid or unstructured, and a figure they cite enters only from a filing or its primary source.

name: Organisations read without a connector
reason: Leaderboards, surveys and research groups the tracker reads for context and leads; their figures enter as hand-entered rows with a verbatim snippet when an indicator needs one.
